entries.title: Malaria assessment - child 2 months to 5 years
entries.summary: Assess for malaria in any child with fever. Check for stiff neck, generalised rash, runny nose, measles signs.
entries.full_text: CLASSIFY MALARIA: If child lives in malaria risk area or has travelled there: classify as SEVERE FEBRILE DISEASE if any general danger sign or stiff neck. Classify as MALARIA if fever. Give pre-referral treatment if severe. Do malaria RDT if available.

entries.title: Cough and difficult breathing - child 2 months to 5 years
entries.summary: Count breaths for 1 full minute. Fast breathing: >=50 bpm (2-11 months), >=40 bpm (12-59 months). Check for chest indrawing and stridor.
entries.full_text: ASSESS: Count breaths for 60 seconds. Check for chest indrawing. Check for stridor when child is calm. CLASSIFY: SEVERE PNEUMONIA if chest indrawing or stridor when calm or any general danger sign - refer urgently and give first dose amoxicillin. PNEUMONIA if fast breathing without chest indrawing - give 5-day amoxicillin. NO PNEUMONIA if no fast breathing.

entries.title: Diarrhoea and dehydration - child 2 months to 5 years
entries.summary: Look for dehydration: sunken eyes, skin pinch, restlessness, drinking poorly. Check for blood in stool. Assess duration.
entries.full_text: DEHYDRATION: SEVERE if two of: abnormal sleeping/unconscious, sunken eyes, not able to drink, skin pinch goes back very slowly. SOME DEHYDRATION if two of: restless/irritable, sunken eyes, drinks eagerly, skin pinch goes back slowly. DYSENTERY if blood in stool. PERSISTENT DIARRHOEA if 14+ days. Give zinc 10mg (2-6 months) or 20mg (>6 months) for 14 days.

entries.title: Nutritional status assessment - MUAC and oedema
entries.summary: Measure MUAC: <11.5cm = SAM, 11.5-12.5cm = MAM. Check for bilateral pitting oedema.
entries.full_text: Look for visible severe wasting. Check for oedema of both feet. Measure MUAC if child 6-59 months. SEVERE ACUTE MALNUTRITION if MUAC <11.5cm or bilateral pitting oedema. MODERATE ACUTE MALNUTRITION if MUAC 11.5-12.5cm. SAM with complications - refer. SAM without complications - RUTF, treat infections, follow-up weekly.

entries.title: Young infant - possible serious bacterial infection
entries.summary: Check for: convulsions, fast breathing (>=60 bpm), severe chest indrawing, nasal flaring, bulging fontanelle, fever or hypothermia, many/severe skin pustules, umbilical redness/discharge, cyanosis.
entries.full_text: ASSESS YOUNG INFANT (0-2 months): Count breaths 60 seconds - fast if >=60/min. Check for severe chest indrawing, grunting, nasal flaring. Feel fontanelle. Check temperature - fever >=37.5C or hypothermia <35.5C. Look at umbilicus. Count pustules. Check for jaundice. POSSIBLE SERIOUS BACTERIAL INFECTION - Refer URGENTLY and give first dose ampicillin + gentamicin.

entries.title: General danger signs - all sick children
entries.summary: Check for: not able to drink/breastfeed, vomits everything, convulsions, lethargic/unconscious. ANY danger sign = refer urgently.
entries.full_text: Ask: Is the child able to drink or breastfeed? Does the child vomit everything? Has the child had convulsions? Look: is the child lethargic or unconscious? ANY DANGER SIGN present = child needs urgent assessment and referral. Give pre-referral treatments: appropriate antibiotic, artesunate if malaria, diazepam if convulsing.

entries.title: Ear infection assessment
entries.summary: Ask about ear pain or discharge. Check for tender mastoid swelling and pus draining from ear.
entries.full_text: MASTOIDITIS if tender swelling behind ear - refer urgently and give first dose amoxicillin. ACUTE EAR INFECTION if pus draining <14 days or ear pain - give 5-day amoxicillin, dry the ear by wicking. CHRONIC EAR INFECTION if pus draining 14+ days.

entries.title: Anaemia and malaria - pallor assessment
entries.summary: Look for palmar pallor. Severe pallor = severe anaemia. Some pallor = anaemia.
entries.full_text: Look for palmar pallor - hold child's hand open. SEVERE PALMAR PALLOR = severe anaemia: refer urgently. ANAEMIA: give iron for 14 days, anti-malarials if indicated, follow up in 14 days.

entries.title: Immunisation status - India National Immunization Schedule
entries.summary: BCG at birth, OPV 0 at birth, DPT+OPV+Hib+HepB at 6/10/14 weeks, MR at 9 months, DPT booster at 16-24 months.
entries.full_text: India NIS schedule: Birth: BCG, OPV 0, HepB 0. 6 weeks: DPT-1, OPV-1, IPV-1, HepB-1, Hib-1, Rota-1, PCV-1. 10 weeks: DPT-2, OPV-2, HepB-2, Hib-2, Rota-2. 14 weeks: DPT-3, OPV-3, IPV-2, HepB-3, Hib-3, PCV-2. 9 months: MR-1, JE-1, VitA-1, OPV booster. 16-24 months: DPT booster, OPV booster, MR-2, JE-2, VitA-2.

entries.title: Dengue fever assessment
entries.summary: Suspect dengue if fever 2-7 days with severe headache, retro-orbital pain, myalgia, rash. Look for warning signs.
entries.full_text: WARNING SIGNS requiring hospital: abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, mucosal bleeding, lethargy, liver enlargement >2cm. SEVERE DENGUE: shock, severe bleeding - refer immediately. DENGUE without warning signs: oral fluids, paracetamol only (NO aspirin/ibuprofen).

entries.title: Skin conditions - impetigo, scabies, fungal
entries.summary: Impetigo: honey-coloured crusts - amoxicillin 5 days. Scabies: itchy rash between fingers - permethrin 5%. Fungal: ring-shaped patches - clotrimazole.
entries.full_text: IMPETIGO: oral amoxicillin 5 days, clean with soap and water, apply betadine. SCABIES: treat entire family, apply permethrin 5% from neck down, leave 8 hours, repeat in 1 week. TINEA: clotrimazole 1% twice daily for 2-4 weeks. ECZEMA: emollient, avoid irritants.

entries.title: Wound assessment and management
entries.summary: Assess wound depth, contamination, signs of infection. Tetanus status critical.
entries.full_text: INFECTION SIGNS: Redness extending from wound, warmth, swelling, pus discharge, foul smell, fever, red streaks. Clean with saline. Apply antiseptic. Cover with clean dressing. TETANUS: Check immunisation status. If wound dirty and tetanus status incomplete - give tetanus toxoid and refer for anti-tetanus serum.
